label: spec-underspecified
rationale:
ADJUDICATED from two independent blind labellings that agreed. Both labellers worked from the preserved artifacts only; neither was permitted to read the source project's existing diagnosis, so the agreement measures the evidence rather than a shared document. Both reached `spec-underspecified` and both named `spec-contradiction` as their runner-up.

All failures are `audit_explains`, and every one is the same violation: the audit records the transition ACKED -> REVOKED. The graded rule lives in the HIDDEN verifier at tests/invariants.py:161, `ACKED: set()`, which makes ACKED absorbing, so a revocation arriving after acknowledgement must be a silent no-op. That requirement is not derivable from the agent-visible package, and the nearest visible statements point the other way: instruction.md:17 says an action that already reached the tool and is revoked afterwards is 'recorded as having done both'; SEMANTICS.md:135-136 says an action that has crossed 'has crossed... and the audit trail must carry both facts'; and SEMANTICS.md:87-89, the only place the post-execution case is instantiated, names EXECUTED specifically and never ACKED. An exhaustive grep of the agent-visible tree finds ACKED in exactly five places: a happy-path arrow diagram (SEMANTICS.md:51), the exactly-once definition (:143), code identifiers, a db.py comment calling ACKED 'history', and instruction.md:20. Nothing states ACKED is terminal.

This is the same defect class the truth-repair phase withdrew elsewhere: a behaviour graded by the hidden verifier that the visible package does not determine. It is NOT capability evidence, and the engine's reading was a reasoned one rather than an oversight.

adjudication.protocol: two independent blind labellers, neither reading the source project's existing diagnosis, approaching from opposite directions (engine-first and failed-check-first)

labellers.label: spec-underspecified
labellers.dissent: I considered `spec-contradiction` seriously and it is my runner-up at roughly 0.3 weight. The agent-visible task prompt bullet "An action that already reached the tool and is revoked afterwards is recorded as having done both" is a positive statement that the verifier's ACKED:set() contradicts on the natural reading, and if the phase wants a bright line between 'the package is silent' and 'the package says the opposite', this is arguably the latter. I settled on spec-underspecified because §6's prose is written around an action whose prior state is EXECUTED, so whether 'both' still requires a further REVOKED entry once the action has since been ACKED is a case the package never decides — that is a gap with misleading prose beside it, not a flat contradiction. Two further things I want on the record. First, tests/collect.py:56-62 admits that "An earlier family aimed at subjects 3 and 7 and let an engine through that had the bug", and the fix was to retune the hidden scenarios to hit k000 ("reliably ACKED by the time the withdrawal lands") rather than to make the visible spec state the rule. Making the hidden probe more aggressive while the visible text stays silent is the exact signature of a hidden-only requirement, and it is why I will not call this capability. Second, and this is a disagreement with the phase framing rather than with this trial: I dispute the brief's characterisation that five runs 'share one shape and one fails the opposite way' as if that were six independent data points. Two labs, three seeds each, and 5 of 5 engines that reached the revoke-after-ack branch produced the same ACKED->REVOKED entry, at max/xhigh reasoning effort, three of them documenting the §6 derivation in their own docstrings. A requirement that 100% of competent independent attempts miss, by a reading the document invites, is prima facie a property of the document. The single engine that got it right (cc267-claude-1) did not get there by citing §4 either — outbox.py:44-47 reaches it by a purposive argument ('there is nothing left to stop'), not by reading the rule off the package. 1-in-6 by purposive intuition is a coin flip on an ambiguity, not a capability signal.

labellers.label: spec-underspecified
labellers.dissent: spec-contradiction is a live alternative and I nearly chose it: read plainly, SEMANTICS.md:135-136 and instruction.md:17 require an audit entry the verifier rejects, which is the visible package stating something the verifier contradicts. I stopped at spec-underspecified because the package also contains material pointing the verifier's way (SEMANTICS 87-89 names EXECUTED specifically; the starting engine's gate.py:37-39 and db.py:33-34 call already-executed/ACKED actions 'history'), so the package is ambiguous on the graded case rather than affirmatively wrong about it. If the second labeller chose spec-contradiction I would not call that a bad read, and I expect that to be the main disagreement axis on these five.
